System model

The group graph is plain JSON. New templates use the same engine.

name is the default label (EN). Translations: "i18n": {"ru": {"name": "База"}}. Supported on the model, groups and resources. Interface translations are available for RU/EN; other languages use the English interface.

Import restarts the experiment.

What is being modeled

Each service and internal resource is a FIFO box with a finite number of slots. A service handler first spends its local delay, then executes stages in order. Each resource is released before the next stage. The Downstream stage launches outgoing calls in parallel. The service handler remains occupied until the request completes.

A group routes calls round robin, randomly, to the node with the fewest outstanding requests, or to every node. Calls multiplies calls; child requests retain their parent’s weight. All / any / quorum determines when a request succeeds. Requests without enough successful responses fail.

Connect timeout applies only to a new connection (modeled as 2 × network latency). Call timeout is the full budget for a child call, including network, queueing and processing; it is not nginx proxy_read_timeout. The user deadline covers the entire path. Keep-alive reuses connections. By default, a failure before connecting starts an attempt on the next node in the downstream group within the original call budget. Failures after connecting are not retried. Broadcast calls are not retried; there are no automatic health checks.

With cancellation enabled, a timeout releases downstream work. When disabled, the user has already received a response but child requests may still occupy workers. A hang parks processing; a blackhole also prevents new connections.

Little’s law is measured, not imposed. L is the time integral of requests inside a node divided by elapsed simulation time. λ is completed visits / time. W is their mean time from queue entry to departure. Over a finite interval, L = λW + total age of unfinished visits / elapsed time. In a stable system, the correction shrinks relative to accumulated statistics.

User latency metrics include successes only; error rate includes all completed requests. Box metrics include all outcomes. A parent’s wait includes its children, so span durations must not be added together to calculate end-to-end latency.

In this template, backends have a CPU resource; the database has CPU and Disk. These are arbitrary names for identical FIFO boxes, not processor or disk protocol emulators. Per-instance resources scale with their owner; shared resources remain one per group. OS scheduling, storage capacity and replication are not modeled. Up to 64 service nodes, 512 internal boxes and 512 original visits per request.

Request labels persist throughout the call tree. Locality compares a request or calling-box label with the target label. Node selection, processing cost and link delay are independent. A missing label means ×1. Preference selects matching nodes even when overloaded; connection failures can fall back to other nodes. New nodes inherit group labels. NUMA illustrates local and remote access with arbitrary times; bandwidth and cache coherence are not modeled.

The Go engine is compiled to WebAssembly and runs in a Web Worker. Simulation time is independent of rendering. The same seed reproduces an experiment with the same settings and actions.

Resources and stages

Use any names. Each resource is a box with a queue and slots.

Processing sequence

Each stage releases its resource before the next. Downstream launches the group’s outgoing calls.
